android.desc:
Gravity Focus is an all-in-one tool designed to help with scheduling, time management, and focus. It brings everything together to help reduce procrastination, difficulties with time management, and missed schedules, while making it easier to organize your day.

Why You Should Use Gravity Focus

1. The app was created by a Korean adult with ADHD who personally experienced challenges such as procrastination and difficulty managing schedules, with the goal of reducing those everyday struggles.

2. Designed to support your entire day, from morning to night
- Start your day with routines
- Plan your daily tasks with a time schedule
- Break tasks into smaller steps and use the Pomodoro technique to reduce pressure and improve focus
- Keep a diary to reflect on your day and identify areas for improvement
- Review time usage reports to see where your time went

3. Supports the Windows platform.
You can install it from the Microsoft Store.

4. Respects your privacy.
- User content (such as schedules and diary entries) is not collected by the developer’s server and is stored locally on your device
- For cross-device sync: synchronization and backup use encryption and your personal Google Drive

show_hn.title: Show HN: Local-First ADHD Planner for Windows and Android (Syncs via GDrive)

quotes.text:
Hello HN,

I am a Physics PhD student. I built this app because I kept procrastinating on my thesis due to ADHD, and existing tools didn't fit my workflow.

Most ADHD apps are either mobile-only or require monthly subscriptions for cloud sync on their proprietary servers. Since I work on a Windows PC in the lab and use an Android phone on the go, I needed a cross-platform solution that respects privacy.

The Solution: I built Gravity Focus using Flutter.

Local-first & Privacy: No central server. Data syncs directly via your own Google Drive (encrypted). I have no access to your data.

Cross-Platform: Windows (MSIX) and Android support.

Methodology: Combines Routine blocking, Pomodoro, and Task Chunking (breaking tasks down to lower resistance).

I released it on the Microsoft Store and Play Store. It’s free to use for basic features. I'd love to get some feedback on the sync architecture or the UX from an ADHD perspective.
